subject: Commercial appendix: pricing cadence, min-commit carveout & VAT evidence - Lumen Health
messages:

To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@lumenhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial appendix: pricing cadence, min-commit carveout & VAT evidence - Lumen Health

Hi team,

Attaching Lumen's latest redline to the Order Form (Lumen_OrderForm_redline_v2.docx) and a short worksheet that maps their requested pricing bands to our pricing ladder. Quick background: Lumen is asking for a 3-band commit with a soft min-commit carveout for months 10-12 and net-60 on initial invoices (they asked for net-90, we pushed back). They also asked us to accept a VAT reverse-charge note for EU billing — Lumen says procurement can provide supporting certificates.

asks:
- Legal: can we accept the "carveout" language that limits minimum commit to active product modules (see §2.1a)? Kimberly, please flag anything that would expose us to an open credit risk.
- Finance: confirm we can do net-60 on first invoice with standard ACH remit thereafter; markus, will this require a change to our revenue recognition or collections playbook?
- Priya: I'll loop you on procurement evidence and rollout plan; want to align on the invoice flow before I send the next draft to Tom.

Attachments: redline, pricing-staircase worksheet, VAT-evidence checklist.

Thanks,
Karthik

-- 
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-29T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial appendix: pricing cadence, min-commit carveout & VAT evidence - Lumen Health

Thanks Karthik — adding Priya's voice: noted. I read through the redline quickly; two operational clarifications from our side before legal/finance deep-dive:

1) Invoice path: Tom asked for a single invoice per quarter for committed spend + usage true-up. Do we want to accept a quarterly billing cadence with monthly usage reporting? That affects how we draft invoice-trigger language.
2) Activation fee: their redline suggests prorating activation across the first 3 invoices; we typically do a one-time upfront activation. If finance is okay with quarterly invoices I can accept prorated activation, otherwise prefer upfront.

Markus / Kimberly — can you review the attached checklist and workbook and call out any items that will block signature? If legal is comfortable with the carveout language in §2.1a, we can push the redline back with net-60 on first invoice and quarterly invoicing thereafter.

Priya

-- 
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@lumenhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial appendix: pricing cadence, min-commit carveout & VAT evidence - Lumen Health

Folks — legal review below (high level). I tracked a few edits in the attached redline (Lumen_OrderForm_redline_v2.docx). Key risks and recommended language: 

1) §2.1a (min-commit carveout): the concept is acceptable if we add a clear definition for "active product modules" and include a 30-day notice window before the carveout applies. Without definition this could be interpreted broadly and erode commit. Proposed insert: "Active Product Modules": product modules provisioned and used for at least 15 days in the prior billing period.

2) Net terms: net-60 on the first invoice is permissible for this deal provided procurement signs the order of magnitude of the commit and we obtain the PO prior to activation. Recommend adding a one-time activation holdback clause up to 10% until PO is received.

3) VAT / reverse charge: do not accept blanket reverse-charge language without evidence. We should accept reverse-charge only if Lumen provides: (a) local tax registration or (b) a valid VAT self-assessment certificate + remit-to entity confirmation. I added a short evidence list in the VAT-evidence-checklist.pdf and a conditional clause in §5.2.

4) Quarterly invoicing: operationally OK, but require a monthly usage report and a 15-day invoice dispute window. Added language to §4.3 and the billing appendix.

If finance confirms the activation/pro rata approach for activation fees, I can push the redline back this afternoon.

-Kimberly

-- 
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial appendix: pricing cadence, min-commit carveout & VAT evidence - Lumen Health

All — quick finance take:

1) Net-60 on first invoice: acceptable if we get a signed PO and procurement SLA that commits to timing. Collections will flag a low-dollar holdback (up to 10%) until PO/credit check clears. We can support quarterly invoicing with monthly usage reporting as long as AR is given 10 business days after invoice issuance to trigger collections.

2) Activation fee treatment: we will accept prorated activation across first three quarterly invoices for this customer only, conditional on a contract note that lists the schedule and that total activation value is < $75k. Anything larger must be paid upfront or via escrow.

3) VAT evidence: finance needs the documents Kimberly mentioned to avoid withholding exposure. If Lumen provides registration/certificate, we accept reverse-charge treatment. If not, we will invoice gross + VAT and they can reclaim locally.

Next steps I propose: Kimberly to finalize the tracked redline with the three conditional clauses (active modules defn, PO holdback, VAT evidence). Priya / Karthik to confirm whether the customer will accept quarterly invoices and the PO timing. If yes, Karthik to send revised redline + short email summary to Tom and procurement with a deadline for evidence (10 business days).

Markus

-- 
Markus Klein
Director, Revenue Operations & Finance
Redwood Inference
